items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: I did some work on Leonard Feather’s book, Earwitness to an Era.” I think it was his last book. And he couldn’t come out to the Institute so he sort of hired me to do some digging and stuff.

ctx.x: Who are the most, I don’t know, short list of the most interesting people you’ve met doing your work?

Well I didn’t meet him, but I did some work for him, long distance work for him. I did some work on Leonard Feather’s book, Earwitness to an Era.” I think it was his last book. And he couldn’t come out to the Institute so he sort of hired me to do some digging and stuff. And he paid me nicely, gave me check and everything. And I knew of him, I

knew about him from reading and all of that and I knew all of the great things he did in terms of promoting the music and everything. And so I was very happy and proud to work for Leonard Feather. As far as meeting other people, Gunther Schuller, I met Gunther Schuller who I thought was one of the nicest people ever. He was doing some work on his book about the Swing Era. He pulled out about a ton of LPs and sat down and listened to these things over and over and over again, which was great. And I really enjoyed…
